must_fix.issue: Repeated 'It is often told' reads as hedging on a skim (raised by 3 personas). Reduce to one honest framing line per section, starting with the church section, which has two in a row, and the FAQ, which repeats it.
r2_lines: The rite in church belongs to the Church, not to family custom. What follows describes it in general terms only; your priest has the final word.

It is often told that the couple stand together on an embroidered rushnyk during the service, and that whoever steps onto it first will have the final say in the marriage. Families enjoy the joke; it is not church teaching.

It is often told that the couple are crowned during the service, with crowns held above or placed on their heads, a moment shared with other Eastern rites. You will find a similar rite described in our guide to [Greek wedding traditions](/expert-advice/greek-wedding-traditions).

The encyclopaedia records that embroidered rushnyky were used in folk rites, particularly for weddings. <!-- fact_108 --> The meanings families give it, such as the story about who steps onto it first, are often told rather than recorded, so ask your own family what theirs means to them.
must_fix.fix: Line 115 becomes the section's single framing line: 'The rite in church belongs to the Church, not to family custom. Keep every fact_ marker. Do not turn any unrecorded custom into a flat factual claim. Net length: roughly minus 5 words.

Your Advisor does not handle church or legal paperwork; that stays with your parish and the relevant authorities.
Your Wedded Advisor can plan the day around the service once the parish has given you its answers, but the church's requirements and paperwork stay between you and your parish.
